'''Andreas Glyniadakis''' (alternate spelling: Gliniadakis, [[Greek language|Greek]]: Ανδρέας Γλυνιαδάκης; born 26 August 1981) is a former Greek professional [[basketball]] player, at a height of {{convert|7|ft|1|in|abbr=on}} tall. During his professional [[sports club|club]] career that started in 1997 and ended in 2020, Glyniadakis played at a [[center (basketball)|center]] position.

During his professional club career, Glyniadakis won two [[EuroLeague]] championships. He first won the EuroLeague championship in [[2000 EuroLeague Final Four|2000]], with the Greek club [[Panathinaikos BC|Panathinaikos Athens]]. He later won the EuroLeague championship in [[2012 EuroLeague Final Four|2012]], with the Greek club [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos Piraeus]]. While he was part of [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greece's national team]], he won the bronze medal at the [[2009 EuroBasket]].

==Professional career==
===Europe===
At the start of his career, Glyniadakis played with the [[youth team]]s of Kydonas of [[Chania]], [[Crete]]. He then started his professional club career with the [[Greek Basket League]] team [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos Athens]]. After playing at Panathinaikos, he moved on to the Greek club [[Peristeri BC|Peristeri Athens]], and then to the Greek club [[AEK Athens B.C.|AEK Athens]].

In May 2007, Glyniadakis signed with the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian A League]]'s [[Virtus Pallacanestro Bologna|Virtus Bologna]]. In September 2007, he returned to AEK Athens. However, he was [[waived]] by the club on 1 October 2007. Glyniadakis then joined the Greek team [[Maroussi BC|Maroussi Athens]]. He was chosen as the [[Most valuable player|MVP]] of the Last 16's Week 1 in the [[ULEB Eurocup 2008–09|EuroCup 2008–09 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/43231/448 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090131062604/http://eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/43231/448 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 31, 2009 |title=Glyniadakis last 16 week 1 MVP |publisher=Eurocupbasketball.com |date=2009-01-28 |access-date=2013-12-26}}</ref>

In July 2009, Glyniadakis moved to the Greek [[EuroLeague]] team [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos Piraeus]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/euroleague/77979/olympiacos-inks-glyniadakis-to-replace-printezis.html Olympiacos inks Glyniadakis to replace Printezis.]</ref> With Olympiacos, he won the EuroLeague and Greek League championships in 2012. After a season of playing for the [[Kazakhstan Basketball Championship|Kazakhstan Championship]] club [[BC Astana|Astana]], Glyniadakis signed with [[BC Lietuvos rytas|Lietuvos rytas]] of the [[Lithuanian Basketball League|Lithuanian LKL League]].<ref>[http://bc.lrytas.lt/en/item/1077-lietuvos-rytas-pens-two-time-champ-aglyniadakis-to-deal Lietuvos rytas pens two-time champ A.Glyniadakis to deal.]</ref>

On 31 January 2014, Glyniadakis signed a contract with [[Cypriot Basketball League|Cypriot Division A]] side [[APOEL B.C.|APOEL]], and he helped the team to win the Cypriot League's championship at the end of the season.<ref>[https://www.eurobasket.com/Cyprus/basketball.aspx?NewsID=356077 Andreas Glyniadakis: "I joined Apoel to win the title"!!]</ref> On 30 October 2014, Glyniadakis was signed by the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League]] team [[Royal Halı Gaziantep]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/139453/andreas-glyniadakis-signs-with-gaziantep.html Andreas Glyniadakis signs with Gaziantep.]</ref> On 23 December 2014, he signed with [[CS Energia Rovinari|Energia Rovinari]] of the [[Romanian Basketball League|Romanian National League]], for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/romania/145919/andreas-glyniadakis-inks-in-romania-with-energia-targu-jiu-rovinari.html Andreas Glyniadakis inks in Romania with Energia Targu Jiu Rovinari.]</ref><ref>[http://www.eurobasket.com/Romania/news/387755/Rovinari-lands-Andreas-Glyniadakis Rovinari lands Andreas Glyniadakis.]</ref>

On 14 August 2015, Glyniadakis signed with [[Les Lions de Geneve]] of the [[Switzerland|Swiss]] [[Championnat LNA]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/switzerland/172707/andreas-glyniadakis-signs-in-switzerland-with-geneve-lions.html Andreas Glyniadakis signs in Switzerland with Geneve Lions.]</ref> In November 2015, he left the Lions, and signed with the Greek club [[Nea Kifissia B.C.|Nea Kifissia]], for the rest of the 2015–16 season.<ref>[http://www.a1basket.gr/2015/11/kifisia-agreed-terms-with-andreas-glyniadakis.html A1Basket.gr Kifisia agreed terms with Glyniadakis.]</ref> On 21 July 2016, Glyniadakis signed with the Greek club [[P.A.O.K. B.C.|PAOK Thessaloniki]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/207127/andreas-glyniadakis-moves-to-paok-thessaloniki.html Andreas Glyniadakis moves to PAOK Thessaloniki.]</ref>

On 4 August 2017, Glyniadakis signed with the Greek club [[Kymis B.C.|Kymis]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/243444/kymis-inks-andrea-glyniadakis.html Kymis inks Andrea Glyniadakis]</ref> On 22 August 2018, Glyniadakis returned to his home land of Crete, after nearly two decades, after he signed a one-year deal with the [[Rethymno Cretan Kings B.C.|Rethymno Cretan Kings]]. Glyniadakis joined the Greek club [[Ilysiakos BC|Ilysiakos Athens]], in 2019, and he retired from playing pro club basketball iun 2020.

===NBA===
Glyniadakis was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]], with the 58th overall pick of the [[2003 NBA draft]]. In the 2005–06 season, he played with the [[Roanoke Dazzle]] of the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]]. He played with the [[Atlanta Hawks]] during the 2006 [[NBA]] preseason, but he was cut before the regular season began. He also played with the [[Albuquerque Thunderbirds]] of the NBA D-League, and with them, he won the [[D-League championship]], in the year 2006.

Glyniadakis was signed by the NBA's [[Seattle SuperSonics]], on 5 November 2006.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2650600 Sonics sign Glyniadakis, adding depth to thin frontcourt.]</ref> With the Sonics, he appeared in 13 regular season games, in which he averaged 1.3 points per game. He was [[waived]] by the Sonics on 4 January 2007.<ref>[http://www.seattletimes.com/sports/sonics-waive-farmer-and-glyniadakis/ Sonics waive Farmer and Glyniadakis.]</ref>

Glyniadakis' final NBA game was played on 2 January 2007 in an 88–112 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. In his last NBA game, he recorded no stats, and only played for a total of 52 seconds, as he was substituted in at the very end of the 4th quarter, for [[Damien Wilkins]]. Glyniadakis also played with the [[Boston Celtics]]'s Summer League squad in the 2007 [[NBA Summer League]], in [[Las Vegas, Nevada]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/summerleagues/celtics_070703.html Summer League: Boston Celtics Roster.]</ref>

==National team career==
Glyniadakis was a member of the Greek junior national teams. With Greece's junior national teams, he played at the [[1997 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]]. He won the bronze medal at the [[1998 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]]. He also played at the [[1999 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]], and at the [[2000 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]].

Glyniadakis was also selected to the senior men's [[Greek national basketball team|Greek national team]] for the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympic Games]]. With Greece, he won the bronze medal at the [[2009 EuroBasket]]. He also played with Greece at the [[2014 FIBA World Cup]].
